title: Modi Interacts With AI Avatar of Swami Chinmayananda at Chinmaya Anniversary
excerpt: The Prime Minister questioned a digital recreation of the late Chinmaya Mission founder during the organisation's 75th anniversary conclave in New Delhi.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with an AI-generated avatar of Swami Chinmayananda, the founder of the Chinmaya Mission who died in 1993, at the Chinmaya Mission's 75th anniversary celebrations in New Delhi.
  • Modi asked the avatar about the Mission's journey and his message for the nation; the digital recreation answered in the late teacher's style and wished that his teachings spread across India.
  • The exchange came during the Chinmaya Sammelan and National Leadership Conclave, where Modi also unveiled a commemorative coin and postage stamp.
  • Chinmaya Mission runs schools, temples and study groups across the diaspora, and the AI demonstration put the Mission's archive at the centre of its anniversary outreach.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has interacted with an artificial-intelligence avatar of Swami Chinmayananda, the Chinmaya Mission founder who died in 1993, in a demonstration that placed a digital recreation of the late spiritual teacher at the centre of the organisation's 75th anniversary celebrations in New Delhi.

In the exchange, Modi asked the avatar about the Chinmaya Mission's journey and about Swami Chinmayananda's message for the nation, according to the Press Information Bureau. The avatar responded in the teacher's manner, describing how Chinmayananda carried Vedanta from village to village and expressing the wish that his message spread across the nation. Hindustan Times, reporting the same interaction, quoted the avatar's line that it was "not AI" but "Atma Intelligence" — a play on the initials that drew attention on social media, where clips of the exchange circulated widely, including from the Hindu's video coverage.

"I am not AI. I am Atma Intelligence."

— AI avatar of Swami Chinmayananda, as reported by Hindustan Times

An anniversary with a technology showcase

The interaction took place during the Chinmaya Sammelan and the National Leadership Conclave on October 17-18, part of the Amrit Mahotsav marking 75 years of the Chinmaya Movement. At the inauguration, Modi also unveiled a commemorative coin and a postage stamp honouring Swami Chinmayananda and the Mission's milestone. The avatar drew on the Mission's extensive archive of Chinmayananda's recorded discourses — the raw material that makes a convincing digital recreation of a teacher possible decades after his death.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2113641096689668488

Why it drew attention

The demonstration lands in a wider Indian debate about digital recreations of the dead: devotional organisations hold deep audio and video archives, and AI voice-and-image tools can now turn those archives into interactive figures. Supporters see a way for new generations to encounter a teacher's words directly; critics ask who controls the script such an avatar speaks, and whether a generated answer can drift from what the person actually taught. The Chinmaya Mission has not presented the avatar as a replacement for its living teachers — it appeared as a set-piece within an anniversary program — but the prime ministerial stage gave the experiment unusual visibility.

The diaspora connection

The Chinmaya Mission is one of the most established Hindu organisations in North America, running Bala Vihar classes, temples and study groups in dozens of US and Canadian cities. For those communities, the anniversary — and its AI centrepiece — is a direct line back to the teacher whose books and camps shaped much of diaspora Hindu education since the 1970s.
